purpose: Inspect archived notification evidence and restore or permanently delete selected archived records.
primaryGoal: Find archived notifications through shareable server-side filters, inspect complete delivery/alert context, and intentionally restore or delete records.

dataSources.ownership: Notification log API. ArchivedPage:38-39 requests archived=true without date, vehicle, limit or offset for the explicitly bounded all-time summary. InboxBody:187-200 independently requests archived=true with URL filters, workspace from/to_exclusive, page size and offset. Hook forwards AbortSignal, preserves query keys and normalizes arrays via safeArray. Backend default sample size and filtering semantics were not inspected.
Independent matching-count source; removes limit/offset while retaining filters. Count unavailable is not zero. No count-only handler execution performed.

Fleet and rule catalogs supply local business filters and metadata maps, not a global vehicle scope. Only data arrays are passed to InboxBody; source loading/error/trust is discarded. Vehicles router registration not read in this bounded audit.

Existing mutation hooks own optimistic read state, invalidation/broadcast and localized success/error toasts. Archived bulk actions are Restore and confirmed Delete only. Opening an unread row can mark it read depending on the existing local preference. No mutation was executed.

Rule-linked notification inspection uses log.id for alert detail and a synthetic fallback summary. Drawer preserves cached detail on refresh error and exposes retry. Equivalence of notification-log IDs and alert IDs is unverified; do not invent a replacement mapping.

findings.detail: Vehicles and rules are reduced to data=[]; loading, fatal errors, refresh errors and retries never reach filter/metadata consumers. NotificationFilterBar:102-115 consequently exposes only All options when catalogs are unresolved/unavailable, without explaining incomplete choices.
findings.fix: Pass existing query trust into the shared domain surface and show source-local loading/unavailable/retry notices while retaining loaded catalogs, unknown IDs and usable notification rows. Do not hide the evidence table on catalog failure.

findings.detail: Fatal matching-count failure is text-only; table pagination at :784-791 is supplied only when countData exists. Pull-to-refresh at :716 refetches the list, not countQuery, leaving no explicit count recovery affordance.
findings.fix: Add source-local count Retry with existing QueryError/InlineCallout pattern and retain rows/loaded counts; do not fabricate a total or silently change page size.

findings.detail: Filtered zero-result archive displays the same 'Archived notifications will appear here' text as a truly empty archive and has no reset-filter action.
findings.fix: Use localized filter-aware no-match explanation and an existing EmptyState action to clear page-specific filters, keeping header workspace range ownership separate.

visualIssues.detail: Metadata dt/dd roles use local text-xs/text-sm classes; table metadata also repeats raw text-xs at NotificationInboxTable:74,104,107,110,163,194,201,223.
visualIssues.fix: Use current Caption/Text semantic render overrides and retain tabular/date/error distinctions; subdued existing CSS text tokens are appropriate and need no new palette.

architectureIssues.detail: Archived route renders the inbox categorization assistant with vehicle/severity/rule IDs only. It receives neither archived=true nor from/to_exclusive, source/read/search, and its supported windowDays prop is omitted. AIInboxAutoCategorization:172-180 stream identity similarly cannot invalidate output when archive/workspace dates change. This proves missing frontend scope propagation, not backend filtering behavior.
architectureIssues.fix: Integration owner must explicitly label the assistant's real independent scope or extend the existing typed AI scope contract after backend verification. Preserve advisory feature and user-applied rule filtering; never silently claim archive-period analysis or add autonomous mutations.

architectureIssues.detail: Archived summary normalizes case/whitespace but counts only severity='warn'; NotificationInboxTable:178-179 explicitly recognizes both warn and warning. A warning row is therefore counted as unknown severity in the summary's attention calculation at :144-147 while the evidence table calls it Warn.
architectureIssues.fix: Agree the existing notification severity alias normalization in the domain owner and apply consistently to sample counts, table badges and drawer tone. Preserve genuine unknown values and raw wire/cache severity; do not rewrite source payloads.

architectureIssues.detail: Drawer statusTone checks 'warning' only, while archive filter/summary use 'warn' and table accepts both; a warn alert receives info tone despite its warning label.
architectureIssues.fix: Reuse the agreed domain severity normalization for tone selection without changing lifecycle state, original severity text, rule semantics or persisted data.
